title: Module flatness over an etale base local ring
statement: Let $e:T\to S$ be an etale morphism of schemes [def-pc-scheme, def-weil-etale-morphism]. Let $t\in T$, put $s=e(t)$, and let $M$ be an $\mathcal O_{T,t}$-module. Regard $M$ as an $\mathcal O_{S,s}$-module through the stalk map $e_t^\sharp:\mathcal O_{S,s}\to\mathcal O_{T,t}$; stalks and scalar actions are as in [def-pc-module-stalk-functor]. Then $M$ is flat over $\mathcal O_{S,s}$ if and only if it is flat over $\mathcal O_{T,t}$, where module flatness is as in [def-weil-pbc-flat-ring-map]. No finiteness assumption on $M$ is imposed.

source.place: Tag 05BA, lemma-etale-flat-up-down-local-ring; proof via Tag 05B9, lemma-etale-flat-up-down.

proof.text: Put $R=\mathcal O_{S,s}$, $A=\mathcal O_{T,t}$, $P=T\times_S T$ with projections $p_1,p_2$, and let $\delta:T\to P$ be the diagonal, so $p_i\delta=\operatorname{id}_T$ [def-pc-fibre-product]. Set $z=\delta(t)$ and $C=\mathcal O_{P,z}$. By [def-weil-etale-morphism] and [def-weil-unramified-morphism], $\delta$ is an open immersion. By [def-weil-open-immersion], it identifies the structure sheaf with its restriction to an open neighbourhood; taking germs gives an isomorphism $d=\delta_t^\sharp:C\to A$. Write $a_i=p_{i,z}^\sharp:A\to C$. Stalk-map composition [def-weil-locally-ringed-space-morphism] gives $d a_i=\operatorname{id}_A$. Since $d$ is invertible, $a_1=a_2=d^{-1}$. Thus both projections have exactly the same scalar action at this diagonal point.

source.place: Tag 05B9, open-diagonal argument, with X=T and its map to T the identity; applied directly to stalks for Tag 05BA.

proof.text: Suppose $M$ is flat over $R$ through $e_t^\sharp$. Apply [lem-pc-pullback-stalk-relative-flat-extension] with both scheme morphisms equal to $e:T\to S$, first-factor point $t$, second-factor point $t$, and fibre-product point $z=\delta(t)$. Its hypothesis is precisely this $R$-flatness of the arbitrary $A$-module $M$; both projection images equal $t$ by Step 1. It yields flatness over the second copy of $A$ of $N=C\otimes_{A,a_1}M$, with the $A$-action on $N$ through $a_2$. This input assumes neither quasi-coherence nor finiteness and applies to our given module itself.

source.place: Tag 05B9, preservation of relative flatness under base change; its stalk-module form supplied by the existing relative-flat-extension node.

proof.text: Define $\phi:N\to M$ by $\phi(c\otimes m)=d(c)m$ and $\psi:M\to N$ by $\psi(m)=1\otimes m$. Balancing for $\phi$ follows from $d(a_1(b)c)m=b\,d(c)m$ for $b\in A$. Both maps are $A$-linear for the second-factor action: $d a_2=\operatorname{id}_A$, and $a_2(b)\otimes m=a_1(b)\otimes m=1\otimes bm$. We have $\phi\psi=\operatorname{id}_M$, and $\psi\phi(c\otimes m)=1\otimes d(c)m=a_1(d(c))\otimes m=c\otimes m$, since $a_1d=\operatorname{id}_C$. Hence $N\cong M$ as $A$-modules. For any injective map of $A$-modules, tensoring this isomorphism and its inverse identifies the tensor maps for $N$ and $M$. The map for $N$ is injective by Step 2; therefore the map for $M$ is injective. This proves $A$-flatness using [def-weil-pbc-flat-ring-map].

source.place: Tag 05B9, restriction to the diagonal open subscheme: explicit tensor and scalar identifications at z, giving the forward implication of Tag 05BA.

proof.text: Conversely suppose $M$ is flat over $A$. The morphism $e$ is flat by [def-weil-etale-morphism]; hence $A$ is flat over $R$ via $e_t^\sharp$ by [def-weil-flat-morphism]. Apply [lem-pc-module-flat-transitive] to $R\to A$ and $M$. It gives flatness of $M$ over $R$ with exactly the scalar restriction in the item. Together with Steps 2-3 this proves the equivalence, for every module $M$ without a finiteness assumption.

source.place: Tag 05B9, first paragraph (etale implies flat and flatness is transitive); reverse implication of Tag 05BA.

proof_origin.place: Tag 05BA, proved by applying the open-diagonal/base-change argument of Tag 05B9 directly to modules over stalks.
